properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 3 at 1:44AM PDT until October 6 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures up to 103 degrees expected with the
warmest temperatures will be located in the southern San Joaquin
Valley. Overnight lows between 70 and 75 degrees expected in the
Sierra Foothills where the thermal belt is strongest.

* WHERE...San Joaquin Valley and Sierra Nevada foothills.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to major risk of heat-related
illnesses for much of the population, especially those without
effective cooling or hydration.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 32 will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...In Minnesota, Northern Cook and Lake and Southern Cook
Counties. In Wisconsin, Price, Bayfield, and Sawyer Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This Advisory is primarily for areas away from
the immediate shorelines as those lakeshore area temperatures only
drop down to the upper 30s where frost is not expected.
properties.instruction: Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Knox, TN
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 3 at 3:59AM EDT until October 3 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Morristown TN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Knox County in east Tennessee...

* WHEN...Until 700 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Knoxville, Farragut, Lake Forest, Bearden, Kimberlin Heights and
Mascot.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Walton and Bay County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 3 at 5:30PM ChST until October 5 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Saipan and Tinian.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) is steadily moving northeast and away from
the Marianas. To the south of Choi-wan, surging monsoon inflow
will maintain wet conditions through Sunday, resulting in 3 to 5
inches of rain for Guam and Rota, and 4 to 6 inches for Tinian
and Saipan during the Watch period.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 3 at 3:23PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TYPHOON CHOI-WAN MOVING NORTHEAST AND AWAY FROM AGRIHAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Warning remains in effect for Alamagan, Agrihan and Pagan
in the CNMI.
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan and
their adjacent waters in the CNMI.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for all of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might be
in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 2 PM ChST, the center of Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) was located near
latitude 19.0N and longitude 145.5E. This was about 20 miles north-
northwest of Agrihan, and about 270 miles north of Saipan. Storm
motion was northeast, 35 degrees, at 7 mph with maximum sustained
winds of 100 mph, becoming a Category 2 typhoon. Choi-wan is expected
to make a slight turn toward the north-northeast with a slight
increase in forward speed through Sunday, moving away from the
Marianas. Choi-wan is forecast to intensify further through tonight,
becoming a Category 3 typhoon tonight.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Typhoon Choi-wan continues to intensify, and is expected to become a
Category 3 typhoon tonight as it continues moving away from the
Marianas and passing near Maug to the northeast. A Typhoon Warning
remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan. Due to the
enhancement of the monsoon surge along the southern peripheries of
Choi-wan, TS conditions are still expected at Tinian, Saipan and
their adjacent waters in the early evening hours tonight, but then
becoming more likely to fall below TS conditions as the night goes
on.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind
conditions associated with Typhoon Choi-wan (26W). Heed the advice
of your local emergency managers and officials, and continue to
monitor forecasts by the National Weather Service office in Tiyan,
Guam. Remain in sturdy shelter until the all clear is given.

Remain in suitable shelter, such as a cave or sturdy concrete
structure. Shelter in place until the all-clear is given.

.WIND INFORMATION...
Typhoon winds of 74 mph or more will continue for Alamagan, Agrihan
and Pagan into this evening as Choi-wan treks north through the
northern CNMI and strengthens further into a Category 3 typhoon. On
either side of the typhoon-force winds, tropical storm force winds of
39 to 73 mph look to continue through at least Sunday morning.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf of 10 to 14 feet along north, south, and west facing
reefs are expected to continue, increasing by several feet during
the time of nearest passage. As Choi-wan continues to strengthen,
dangerous surf is likely along all reefs at all three islands through
at least Sunday. Significant coastal erosion and some coastal
inundation is expected during Choi-wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of torrential rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered
thunderstorms are expected through tonight, producing rainfall totals
of 8 to 14 inches by early Monday morning, with up to 20 inches of
rainfall possible near the center of the system.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Alabama, including the following
areas, Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Baldwin Inland, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal and Mobile Inland and northwest Florida,
including the following areas, Escambia Coastal, Escambia Inland,
Okaloosa Coastal, Okaloosa Inland, Santa Rosa Coastal and Santa
Rosa Inland.

* WHEN...From 10 AM CDT Saturday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall are expected Saturday through
at least Sunday afternoon. Additional rainfall amounts of 4 to 6
inches are expected with locally higher amounts of up to 10
inches possible. This may lead to flash flooding, especially in
urban and poor drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the low-80s to
low-90s. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will limit
overnight relief.

* WHERE...The Marin Hills, Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco, and
Northern Salinas Valley/Hollister Valley and Carmel Valley.

* WHEN...From 11 AM Saturday to 10 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Mexico...

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

will begin to threaten several homes and structures in the village
of San Francisco between Interstate 25 and the Rio Grande. Further

- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.

at 9:00 PM MDT Friday was 19.7 feet.

tomorrow afternoon.

feet on 08/10/2006.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/emergencyprepflood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to dip from Minor Flood
Stage to Action Stage this weekend. Towards the middle of next week,
another rise into Minor Flood Stage is forecast due to increasing
rain chances and a return of northerly winds.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.0 feet, River levels rise and fills canals,
encroaching on docks, yards and boat ramps in the vicinity of
SR-40. Properties in low areas along and near the river and many
canals should prepare for further water encroachment. At 2.3 feet,
Many docks become submerged along the river and in canals in the
Astor community. Water enters yards of properties on Bartram Road,
Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road on the Lake County side. In
Volusia County, water encroaches yards of homes on the river side
of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in effect from near the South
Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet south of the Riverview lodge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Friday was 2.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to remain near Minor Flood Stage
through early this weekend, then fall into Action Stage late this
weekend into early next week. The river is then expected to rise
back into Minor Flood Stage into the middle of next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.5
feet on 05/28/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County Southeast; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 2 at 1:42PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...In Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Oct 3 6AM to Midnight.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT DUE TO HARMFUL PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS FROM WINDBLOWN DUST

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 12:54PM MST until October 3 at 2:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by earlier excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River at Birdsprings.

* WHEN...Until 215 AM MST /315 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River near Birdsprings is
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1241 PM MST /141 PM MDT/, water levels on the Little Colorado
River at Winslow have fallen below Action Stage and will continue
to recede. Flooding will remain a threat downstream of Winslow in
Birdsprings. Water levels at Birdsprings are expected to peak
around 9 PM MST /10 PM MDT/, and begin to recede around 11 PM MST
/midnight MDT/.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 12:00pm MST /1:00pm MDT/ the stage was 15.99 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. Minor lowland
overflow on right bank at Winslow.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Birdsprings.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
